newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end firm but off day's high.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end firm but off day's high.

text.p: French shares closed with a gain of more than one percent but off the day's best levels.

Traders said prices retreated in the late afternoon as the Dow softened and the dollar consolidated some of its gains. Earlier, the CAC-index soared 2.18 percent, buoyed by buying on the first day of the monthly account.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 33.41 points or 1.31 percent at 2,587.13, but it was down 2.21 percent on the week. The CAC-40 futures contract closed up 31 at 2,588 from Thursday's close.
Volume was a relatively light 5.86 billion francs.
The bourse's outlook hinges on the decisions made on Tuesday by the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy-making committee, traders said.

They said a quarter-point rise in U.S. interest rates was priced into equities after Fed chairman Alan Greenspan's remarks indicating the central bank could act pre-emptively to guard against inflation.

* Appliance manufacturer SEB surged 7.72 percent at 1,018 francs on plans to buy Arno of Brazil. Several brokers turned buyers on the news, including Cheuvreux de Virieu, SGE Delahaye and Paribas Capital Markets.

* S&P confirmed SEB's short-term T1 rating on SEB's treasury bill programme. It said SEB could absorb Arno without damaging its financial situation and the acquisition would boost its position in a highly competitive industry.
The news lifted appliance maker Moulinex on the back of SEB's gains, closing up 6.5 percent at 131 francs in thin volume, however.
* Credit Lyonnais certificates surged 7.37 percent to 204 francs on better than expected 1996 results. "One has the feeling Credit Lyonnais can rebound," said Transbourse analyst Patrick Leguil.
* Renault rose 2.68 percent to 141.70 francs. It reported a 5.25 billion franc loss for 1996 but analysts said its pre-exceptional operating loss was not as great as feared.
SGE Delahaye raised its recommendation to neutral from underperform, and Exane to reinforce from sell.
* Tobacco company Seita fell 2.27 percent to 206.80 francs. Traders cited U.S. cigarette firm Liggett's admission that smoking was addictive and could cause cancer.
Seita said on Thursday that it planned to cut 300 jobs within 17 months.
